scenario: [LNUL.4.9] `is not` is ONE operator and not `is` applied to a negated subject — the case where the two readings differ observably. Drives the negated eval arm (IsTestExpr.negated with subject IS_SUBJECT_TRUE) over an Int slot. Read correctly as `(f.n) is-not (true)`: the tag is Int, `is true` is false, the negation makes it true, the rule FIRES. Read as `f.n is (not true)` — i.e. `is false` — the tag is still Int, the answer is false, and the rule does NOT fire. An Int operand is what separates them; a Bool operand would fire under both readings and pin nothing. [LGRA] closes this at the grammar (the subject is not an expression position, so `not true` cannot appear there), and this vector pins that the RUNTIME applies the negation after the test rather than to the subject. fact_count 2.
rules_ds:
schema Flag scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    n: Int? mutable

schema Marker scope logical:
    entity_id: String key

rule r:
    Flag f where f.n is not true
->
    emit Marker logical entity_id: f.entity_id
